_how: Each node is one stretch of talk. 'say' is a list of text boxes. Then 'choices' (a menu), 'ask' (a text box: see finds), 'next' (another node), or nothing (the talk ends). Markup: [red]..[/] [yellow] [blue] [gray] [gold] [shake] [wave], ^1-^9 pauses, \n new line. A line can be {"text": "..", "face": "smile", "speed": 60} to swap to art/wonder-smile.svg (once that art exists and is listed in wonder.js) or type slower. Faces: smile, angry, point; each talks on its own using its -talk1/-talk2 art. A line wrapped in (parentheses) is narration: no nameplate, in italics. 'name' is the nameplate; a line or node can set its own "name". A choice can have "needs": "nodeId" (only shows once that node was heard; "!nodeId" means NOT heard yet) and "once": true (hides after it's been picked). 'returning' is where he starts for someone who has talked to him before. FINDS: a node with "ask": "nodeId" opens a text box after its lines. What the visitor types (any case, extra spaces ignored) is looked up in 'finds' ("WHAT THEY TYPE": "nodeId"); several codes can point at the same node. No match goes to 'findMiss'. An empty answer or Esc goes back to the 'ask' node. A node can have "repeat": "nodeId" (if they've already heard this node, he says that one instead) and "flag": "name" (sets a shared rp_flags flag, the same ones the frequency scanner and RFT use). ITEMS (see /items.json): a node can have "give": "itemId" (puts it in their drawer when he says that node) or "takeItem": "itemId" (takes it away, for trades). A choice can have "has": "itemId" (only shows if it's in their drawer; "!itemId" = only if it isn't). NAMEPLATE: once the rp_flags flag in 'knownFlag' is set (by hearing find_cedar), the nameplate reads 'knownName' instead of 'name'. A choice "has": "*" shows if their drawer has anything in it.
_note: DRAFT LINES, except the opening greeting (the user's). Wonder speaks in about 80% caps. Everything else is a placeholder by Claude; rewrite freely. He speaks on his own the first time someone arrives (autoStart in wonder.js).
